title: create / get / update / delete semantics
description:
1. `Engine::call(&OpRequest { model, op, args, options }, &Identity) -> OpResult { data, errors, next_token }` for `get`, `create`, `update` and `delete`.
2. `create`:
   - fills `id` with a uuid v4 if absent;
   - sets `createdAt` and `updatedAt` (ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds) and `__typename`;
   - validates types from the contract (required fields, enums, `AWSDateTime`, `AWSJSON`, `AWSEmail`, `AWSURL`, …).
3. `update` is partial: given fields change, and `null` removes a field.
4. `delete` returns the deleted item.
5. A duplicate create, or an update or delete of a missing record, gives `DynamoDB:ConditionalCheckFailedException`. `get` of a missing record gives `data: null` with no errors.
6. Errors are `{message, errorType}` in `errors`; data errors never panic.
7. Specs cover every row of the §2.2 table for these operations.

Part of the `virtuus-amplify` crate (`rust/crates/virtuus-amplify`; workspace member; `@rust-only` specs in `features/amplify/`; cucumber runner in the crate; 100% coverage). Semantics: `~/Projects/Ripple/design/storage.md` **§2.2**, matching Amplify/AppSync behaviour exactly.
- **Contract format:** `~/Projects/Ripple/contract/contract.schema.json` (vendor a copy into the crate).
- **Fixture:** `features/amplify/fixtures/blog.contract.json`, hand-written in that format and shared by V8 and V9. It has `Blog`; `Post` with owner auth, an enum `status`, a customType `meta`, a hasMany `comments` and an index `postsByBlog` (partition `blogId`, sort `createdAt`); `Comment` with belongsTo `post`; and `Tag` with a composite identifier `["postId", "name"]`.

---
**Repo:** `~/Projects/Virtuus`, branch `feature/amplify-engine` (don't switch branches).
**Rules (Virtuus `AGENTS.md`):** specs before code (Gherkin in `features/`; register new folders in `python/behave.ini` `paths`); 100% coverage in both languages; Python/Rust parity for core behaviour (`make check-parity`); `black`, `ruff`, `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`; Sphinx docstrings / `///` docs on public items; no line comments.
**Toolchain:** `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH` first (a Homebrew cargo 1.81 shadows rustup). Python: `.venv/bin/python` at the repo root.
**Gate:** `make check PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python` green. Baseline on 2026-09-24: 824 behave steps, 100% coverage, parity OK.
**Protocol:** as in Apricitus initiative `apricitus-e70662` (run `kbs show apricitus-e70662` in `~/Projects/Ripple`). Log with `kbs comment` from `~/Projects/Virtuus`; label `ready-for-review` when done; never commit, push, close, or publish.

comments.text:
Added scope (storage-lead), found via Apricity T12: **Engine persistence is broken in two ways.**
1. `Engine::open(Some(dir))` passes the **same** `directory` to every model's `Table::new` (lib.rs ~549, `directory.clone()`), so Clip, Slice and Marker records all land mixed in one folder. Each model gets its own folder: `dir.join(model_name)`.
2. After `add_gsi`, existing records on disk are never loaded or indexed, so a **reopened** engine's GSIs return nothing. After registering all GSIs for a table, call Virtuus's `table.warm()` (table.rs:672) or `load_from_dir` (whichever indexes existing files; read table.rs) so reopening restores indexes.
Scenario (crud.feature or a new persistence.feature): open an engine on a temp dir, create a Blog and two Posts, drop the engine, open a **new** engine on the same dir, then `get` a Post by id returns it and querying `postsByBlog` returns both, ordered. Also assert that the per-model folders exist.
